chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from some of the Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
When he intended to shorten his hair for the Umrah, the barber intended to take from the sides of the head, so he said to him, 'Begin with the forehead,' and so he began with it.

key_terms.النَّاصِيَةِ: The forehead / the center of the forehead

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order for trimming hair during Umrah according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the preferred method for hair removal during Umrah, emphasizing the significance of the nāsīyah (forehead) as the starting point, a practice often linked to the Prophet’s tradition. It highlights the meticulous attention to ritual purity and order in Shia fiqh, where specific sequences in acts of worship are derived from the Imams' practical guidance. This detail underscores the scholarly emphasis on following the exact manner prescribed by the Ahl al-Bayt to ensure the validity and completeness of the pilgrimage rites.
